source: RFC 0007 §14.2 (DR1-F-3, DR1-F-4, RC review round 1 area F; design confirmed by the maintainer's coordinator, 2026-11-23; DR2-F-2, RC review round 2 areas E to H; DR2-E-4)
statement: What a control call works on that no cache keeps is held to a budget of an eighth of the heap, a quarter of what HeapBudget leaves, weighed before the work by a size known already: a body that carries a document, its bytes times the measured tree factor and the candidate's eight; a document the cache will not keep, its stored size times twelve. Work is charged to the tenant of whoever asks for it, whichever document it reads: a tenant's explain at the platform's or an app's revisions is the tenant's, never the platform's (DR2-F-2). Work at most a small body's tree weighs passes without it, and one call counts at most the budget in all, its pieces together: the heaviest call fits alone, whatever its pieces. The host has one budget, which its operators' and service API, the in-process facade, the control plane's reads and the lock-out check all hold their work in. A call that does not fit waits, its tenant's turn round-robin with the other tenants', first in first out within a tenant, no later call passing a waiting one, each tenant taking at most half the budget while another waits unless it holds nothing, for at most half the pipeline's timeout (StageBudgets.workWait), and is otherwise refused 503 with Retry-After before it reads or decides anything. A call already holding budget never waits: what it needs more is granted at once or refused. A route whose path names the document applies the hard rule before it holds anything or reads the body. A call that reads a document's open changes reads them one at a time and keeps of each only what it needs, so they are never all decoded at once: before a record is decoded it is weighed by the bytes it is stored with times four, and the call holds the heaviest so far, never their sum; a record within what passes free holds nothing, as most do; a store that cannot tell a record's size before decoding it (the default of ControlStore.eachOpenChange) has each weighed as a record at the change record cap. The bytes of the record being read are in memory unweighed for a moment: at most one record's, of one call (DR2-E-4).
